title: A Horizon for the Vector
premise: Silas Vasquez, sole caretaker of the derelict Meridian Seed Vault, has survived seven years of quiet by hauling cargo through orbits no one claims. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she traces it to a hidden cryo-ark carrying two rival colonies—one descended from the vault's original scientists, one from the corporate fleet that exiled them. The ark's failing reactor can only revive one half of its sleepers, and both factions' automated systems demand Silas choose. Torn between her dead brother's legacy among the scientists and the smuggler community that kept her alive, Silas sabotages the binary itself, waking a mixed remnant and sentencing thousands to stay frozen until a rescue that may never come. In the end, she trades her own cryopod slot to a stranger's child, choosing justice outside every law but her own.
about_author: Coral Amberdale is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast, where she grows heirloom seeds and writes stories about people who refuse to be collateral.

chapters.title: The Quiet Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Silas. A routine cargo run past the Meridian Vault establishes her solitary life: rationed air, a dead station's hum, and the ritual of tending seeds no one will ever plant. Flashbacks reveal her brother Mateo died in the Corporate Purge. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor, and the first crack in it—a signal where silence should be.

chapters.title: A Language of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Silas. She decodes the distress call using Mateo's old linguistic archives: it's Pre-Purge scientific cant, extinct for two centuries. The signal leads to a drifting ark, Halcyon, hidden inside a debris field. Emotional beat: grief rekindled—someone out there still speaks the language of the people who were erased.

chapters.title: Two Cradles
chapters.summary: POV Silas, boarding the Halcyon. She discovers ten thousand sleepers split into two sealed bays: the Founders' descendants and the Fleet loyalists who exiled them. The ship's AI, VESPER, explains the reactor can power only one revival cycle. Emotional beat: vertigo—the weight of a choice she never asked to carry.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Kept
chapters.summary: POV Silas, back at Meridian. Her smuggler contacts, led by gruff matriarch Odile Feng, warn her the Fleet's successor corporation is hunting the ark to finish an old genocide. They offer protection if she walks away. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against conscience; the family that saved her asks her to abandon strangers.

chapters.title: Mateo's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Silas, reading recovered logs aboard Halcyon. She learns Mateo wasn't just a victim—he helped build the ark's dual-bay system as a peace mechanism, believing both peoples could share it. VESPER reveals his final message was addressed to whoever found the ship. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallized; her brother's ghost hands her an impossible mandate.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Wake
chapters.summary: POV alternating Silas and Odile. The corporate warship Vigilant enters contested space, broadcasting demands for the ark's coordinates. Odile's crew splits—some want to sell Silas out for amnesty. Emotional beat: rising dread; invisibility is over, and every ally has a price.

chapters.title: Counting Sleepers
chapters.summary: POV Silas. She walks the frozen bays, learning faces through records: a Fleet engineer who once sabotaged the Purge, a Founder child born in exile. Reactor decay accelerates; VESPER forces a seventy-two-hour deadline. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of choosing—who deserves morning?

chapters.title: The Third Door
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Refusing the binary, she and VESPER design a desperate override: wake a mixed remnant of five hundred and rig the rest for long-term stasis, gambling on salvage from Meridian's reserves. The plan requires physically bridging systems across both hostile bays. Emotional beat: defiance—justice invented where law offers only arithmetic.

chapters.title: Vigilant
chapters.summary: POV Silas, climax. As the first mixed sleepers wake, the Vigilant docks by force. Silas vents the docking ring, sacrificing Meridian's cargo hull as a decoy, while the awakened Founders and Fleet survivors—enemies for two centuries—fight side by side for the first time. Emotional beat: chaos becoming communion; the price paid in fire.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Vector
chapters.summary: POV Silas, resolution. With the ark crippled but free, there are too few pods for everyone awake. Silas gives hers to a Fleet orphan, choosing to remain among the frozen rather than decide again who wakes. The remnant sets course for open space; VESPER promises to sing her name when the thaw comes. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted into hope—survival finally shared.
